results.title: Residue of a rational number modulo an integer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$ and a rational number $x = a/b$ in lowest terms with $b > 0$, the residue of $x$ modulo $m$ is the element $a \cdot b^{-1}$ of $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$. When $b$ is prime to $m$, $b^{-1}$ is the inverse of $b$ modulo $m$, so the residue is the class $c$ with $b c \equiv a \pmod m$; for other $x$ the inverse, and hence the residue, is a conventional value with no arithmetic meaning.

results.title: The sign sequence $a_{p,l}$

results.title: Existence and uniqueness of the sequence $b_{l,s}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $l$ be an even natural number and $s$ a natural number with $s \le l$ such that $2s + 1$ and $l + 1$ are coprime. results.title: FKG inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The FKG inequality (Fortuin, Kasteleyn, Ginibre 1971). Let `π` be a probability weight on `ConfigSpace E` (`π ≥ 0`, `∑ π = 1`) satisfying the FKG lattice condition. Then any two monotone functions `f g : ConfigSpace E → ℝ` are positively correlated: `E_π[f] * E_π[g] ≤ E_π[f * g]`.

results.title: FKG inequality for increasing events
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The FKG inequality for events: under a probability weight `π` satisfying the FKG lattice condition, two increasing events are positively correlated, `π(A) * π(B) ≤ π(A ∩ B)`.

results.title: Holley inequality for increasing events
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Holley inequality for increasing events (Holley 1974). If `μ₁, μ₂ ≥ 0` have equal total mass and satisfy `μ₁ a * μ₂ b ≤ μ₁ (a ⊓ b) * μ₂ (a ⊔ b)`, then `μ₁(A) ≤ μ₂(A)` for every increasing event `A`. This is Mathlib's `holley` applied to the indicator of `A`.

results.title: Finite measure with prescribed point masses
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The finite measure `∑_ω μ(ω) δ_ω` on `ConfigSpace E` with point masses `μ(ω)` (negative masses are truncated to `0`). For a normalized nonnegative `μ` it is the measure of the `PMF` `PMF.ofFintype μ`; see `measOfMass_eq_toMeasure`.

results.title: Normalized point masses give the probability mass function's measure
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For a normalized nonnegative mass function, `measOfMass μ` is the measure of the `PMF` `PMF.ofFintype (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ μ)`.

results.title: Holley's inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `μ₁, μ₂ ≥ 0` on `{0,1}^E` have equal total mass and satisfy the Holley lattice condition `μ₁(a) μ₂(b) ≤ μ₁(a ∧ b) μ₂(a ∨ b)`, then `measOfMass μ₁` is stochastically dominated by `measOfMass μ₂`. Strict positivity, assumed in Holley's paper, is not needed. See R. Holley, *Remarks on the FKG inequalities*, Comm. Math. Phys. 36 (1974); the real-valued form is `StatMech.holley_dominates`, from Mathlib's `holley`.

results.title: Holley's coupling theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `μ₁, μ₂` are strictly positive probability mass functions on `{0,1}^E` satisfying the Holley lattice condition `μ₁(a) μ₂(b) ≤ μ₁(a ∧ b) μ₂(a ∨ b)`, there is a finite measure on pairs with marginals `measOfMass μ₁` and `measOfMass μ₂`, concentrated on `{(a, b) | a ≤ b}`. See R. Holley, *Remarks on the FKG inequalities*, Comm. Math. Phys. 36 (1974), and G. Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 2.

results.title: Diophantine numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real number $\alpha$ is Diophantine when there are real numbers $\gamma > 0$ and $\tau \ge 0$ such that $|\alpha - p/q| \ge \gamma / q^{2 + \tau}$ for every integer $p$ and every integer $q \ge 1$.

results.title: Real-analytic circle diffeomorphisms
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A real-analytic orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle is given by a lift $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ together with an inverse lift $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, both real-analytic on all of $\mathbb{R}$, such that for every real $x$ we have $F(x + 1) = F(x) + 1$, $G(x + 1) = G(x) + 1$, $G(F(x)) = x$ and $F(G(x)) = x$, and $F$ is strictly increasing.

results.title: Rotation number of a lift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function, and for a natural number $n$ write $F^n$ for the $n$-th iterate of $F$. Then $F$ has rotation number $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ when, for every real $x$, $(F^n(x) - x)/n$ tends to $\alpha$ as $n$ tends to infinity.

results.title: Analytic conjugacy to a rotation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is analytically conjugate to the rotation by $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ when there is a real-analytic circle diffeomorphism with lift $H$ such that $H(F(x)) = H(x) + \alpha$ for every real $x$.

results.title: Herman's analytic linearization problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is an irrational real number $\alpha$ that is not Diophantine such that, for every real-analytic circle diffeomorphism whose lift $F$ has rotation number $\alpha$, $F$ is analytically conjugate to the rotation by $\alpha$.

results.title: Herman's analytic linearization problem has a positive answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is an irrational real number $\alpha$ that is not Diophantine such that, for every real-analytic circle diffeomorphism whose lift $F$ has rotation number $\alpha$, $F$ is analytically conjugate to the rotation by $\alpha$.

results.title: Li's lemma: reconstruction from the largest part and pairwise products

results.title: Li's theorem: partitions are determined by their pairwise products

results.title: The discrete partition is noncrossing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the discrete partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, whose blocks are the singletons, is noncrossing.

results.title: The indiscrete partition is noncrossing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the indiscrete partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the coarsest partition of this set, is noncrossing.

results.title: Discrete noncrossing partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the discrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the finest partition of this set, whose blocks are the singletons $\{a\}$ for $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$; it is noncrossing.

results.title: The indiscrete noncrossing partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the coarsest partition of this set: its only block is the whole set when $n > 0$, and it has no blocks when $n = 0$. It is noncrossing.

results.title: The block of a point in the discrete noncrossing partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the block containing $a$ in the discrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the singleton $\{a\}$.

results.title: The block of a point in the indiscrete noncrossing partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the block containing $a$ in the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is the whole set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: The discrete noncrossing partition consists of the singletons
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the set of blocks of the discrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is exactly the set of singletons $\{a\}$ with $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: The indiscrete partition of the empty set has no blocks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n = 0$, the set of blocks of the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the empty set, is empty.

results.title: The discrete partition of the empty set has no blocks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n = 0$, the discrete noncrossing partition of the empty set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has no blocks: its set of blocks is empty.

results.title: The indiscrete partition of a nonempty set has a single block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ with $0 < n$, the set of blocks of the indiscrete noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $\{\{0, \dots, n-1\}\}$: its only block is the whole set.

results.title: Characterization of the discrete noncrossing partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A noncrossing partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ equals the discrete noncrossing partition if and only if $P$, viewed as a set partition, is the finest partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: Characterization of the indiscrete noncrossing partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A noncrossing partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ equals the indiscrete noncrossing partition if and only if $P$, viewed as a set partition, is the coarsest partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: A partition whose blocks are all the whole set is indiscrete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. If for every $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the block of $P$ containing $a$ is the whole set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, then $P$ is the indiscrete noncrossing partition.

results.title: The empty set has a unique noncrossing partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n = 0$, every noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the empty set, equals the indiscrete noncrossing partition of this set.

results.title: Discrete and indiscrete partitions agree on the empty set

results.title: The only noncrossing partition of the empty set is the discrete one

results.title: Blow-up of a hypergraph along a map

results.summary: Let $D$ be a family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$, let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\varphi : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, m-1\}$. results.title: Instances of TOTAL DOMINATING SET
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges, and a natural number $K$, the bound.

results.title: Graph of a total dominating set instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The graph of an instance $(n, E, K)$ of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$. Loops are dropped, and pairs with an endpoint at least $n$ contribute no edge.

results.title: Well-formed total dominating set instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reversal $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.

results.title: Feasibility of a total dominating set instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of TOTAL DOMINATING SET is feasible when there is a set $S$ of at most $K$ vertices of its graph such that every vertex $v$ of the graph, including the vertices of $S$, is adjacent to some vertex $u \in S$.

results.title: The decision problem TOTAL DOMINATING SET
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: TOTAL DOMINATING SET accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of triples of a natural number, a list of pairs of natural numbers and a natural number, to an instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and feasible: some set of at most $K$ vertices of the graph of the instance contains a neighbor of every vertex. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: TOTAL DOMINATING SET is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem TOTAL DOMINATING SET belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to TOTAL DOMINATING SET by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of the Gödel numbering. results.title: Effective enumeration of oracle codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The $n$-th oracle code is the code that the computable decoder of the Gödel numbering of oracle codes assigns to $n$, or the basic code $\mathtt{zero}$ (the constant $0$ program) when $n$ is not the number of any code. Because the decoder inverts the Gödel numbering, this is an effective enumeration tied to that numbering, not an arbitrary countable encoding.

results.title: The effective enumeration is a left inverse of the Gödel numbering

results.title: The Gödel encoding of oracle codes is primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Regard oracle codes as coded by their Gödel numbers, with the computable decoder as decoding. Then the map sending each oracle code to its Gödel number is primitive recursive.

results.title: The Gödel decoder of oracle codes is primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Regard oracle codes as coded by their Gödel numbers. Then the computable decoder, which sends a natural number $n$ to the oracle code with Gödel number $n$ when there is one and to no value otherwise, is primitive recursive as a map from natural numbers to optional oracle codes.

results.title: The effective enumeration of oracle codes is primitive recursive

results.title: Fuel bounds the inputs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every oracle $o$, fuel $k$, oracle code $c$ and input $n$, if the fuel-indexed evaluator with fuel $k$ returns a value on $c$ and $n$ relative to $o$, then $n < k$.

results.title: Evaluation of oracle codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $o$ be an oracle that assigns to each natural number either a natural number or no value, $c$ an oracle code and $n$ a natural number. The value of $c$ on $n$ relative to $o$ is the value returned by the fuel-indexed evaluator of $c$ on $n$ relative to $o$ at the least fuel $k$ for which that evaluator returns a value; it is undefined when there is no such $k$.

results.title: The Turing jump
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$, the Turing jump $P'$ is the predicate that holds at $n$ exactly when the $n$-th oracle code in the effective enumeration of oracle codes, evaluated with the oracle that answers $1$ at $m$ if $P(m)$ holds and $0$ otherwise, halts on input $n$. Thus $P'$ is the diagonal halting set of the universal oracle machine with oracle $P$.

results.title: Turing reducibility of predicates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is Turing reducible to a predicate $Q$ on the natural numbers when the characteristic function of $P$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $Q$, that is, partial recursive relative to an oracle for the characteristic function of $Q$.

results.title: Turing equivalence of predicates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two predicates $P$ and $Q$ on the natural numbers are Turing equivalent when the characteristic function of $P$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $Q$ and the characteristic function of $Q$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $P$.

results.title: Turing degree of a predicate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Turing degree of a predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is the Turing degree of its characteristic function, that is, the class of the characteristic function of $P$ under Turing equivalence of partial functions $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Turing reducibility is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is Turing reducible to itself.

results.title: Turing reducibility is transitive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For predicates $P$, $Q$ and $R$ on the natural numbers, if $P$ is Turing reducible to $Q$ and $Q$ is Turing reducible to $R$, then $P$ is Turing reducible to $R$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Rabin–Karp reports offsets in increasing order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and lists of natural numbers $P$ and $T$, the offsets returned by Rabin–Karp matching of $P$ in $T$ form a strictly increasing list; in particular no offset is reported twice.

results.title: Rabin–Karp matching with the empty pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and list of natural numbers $T$, Rabin–Karp matching of the empty pattern in $T$ returns the list $[0, 1, \dots, |T|]$ of all offsets from $0$ to $|T|$ in increasing order, at counted cost $0$.

results.title: Rabin–Karp matching with a pattern longer than the text
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and lists of natural numbers $P$ and $T$ with $|T| < |P|$, Rabin–Karp matching of $P$ in $T$ returns no offsets, at counted cost exactly $1 + 2(|P| - 1) + 6|T|$.

results.title: Rabin–Karp offsets on repeated-symbol words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$, symbol $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $m \le n$, Rabin–Karp matching of the pattern $a^m$ in the text $a^n$ (the lists of $m$ and of $n$ copies of $a$) returns $[0, 1, \dots, n - m]$, that is, every shift in increasing order, including overlapping ones.

results.title: Matching cost of Rabin–Karp on repeated-symbol words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d$ be a base, $q > 0$ a modulus, $a$ a natural number and $m$, $n$ natural numbers with $0 < m \le n$. Let $C$ be the counted cost of Rabin–Karp matching with base $d$ and modulus $q$ of the pattern $a^m$ in the text $a^n$ (the lists of $m$ and of $n$ copies of $a$), minus $8m - 1$, with subtraction truncated at $0$. Then $m(n - m + 1) \le C \le 10\,m(n - m + 1)$.
